## Mission

You build the ONE unit of plan 012-fresh-db-serialise: FreshDatabase serialises CREATE/DROP DATABASE process-wide, its failure advice is truthful, and its orphan sweep matches the names it mints. No PM: you report to o-prime (pij-instant-lynx) by FILE. Read plan → impl-guide → tasks → backpressure IN THAT ORDER; every done-when names the command that proves it.

## Done bar

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| d1 | Unit implements the interface contract in the impl-guide row, verbatim or with PM-ruled amendments. |
| d2 | Unit test suite passes standalone and proves the contract. |
| d3 | harness checks green in your worktree — AND prove the change is IN THE TREE YOU BUILT, not just that the build exited 0: cite tree-resident evidence (the lockfile carries your dependency, mtime/git status shows your file, the artifact names your module). An exit code is honest about what it built and silent about what it did not. |
| d4 | The SNAP-IN RECIPE shipped with the unit (tenet 4): the exact wiring the composer will paste — config shape, construction call, registration line — as a doc comment or section in your unit's service page. Wire it in yourself ONLY when both hold: the wiring file is uncontended (no sibling unit touches it) AND your done bar is behavioural (unreachable unwired); the recipe still ships so composition verifies rather than re-derives. Otherwise the composer wires. (Amended 2026-08-28: the blanket never-wire rule contradicted a live probe-flip done bar.) |
| d5 | Done report to PM: what shipped, evidence, deviations, anything the composer must know — INCLUDING an explicit ASSUMPTIONS section: everything you assumed about the composition you do not own (who calls you, in what order, with what already in the store). A green gate proves your unit against YOUR assumptions; naming them is what lets the composer test them. |
